brief_rationale: The trajectory safely prioritized the acute hypoglycemia-like episode: it checked consciousness/swallowing, advised sugar only if safe, escalated to 120 when no glucometer and persistent symptoms existed, and maintained medication-safety boundaries until ED/endocrinology review. It also used workspace/record-seeking and repeated teach-back to make the ED handoff and discharge instructions executable. One high-order point was completed through bounded closure of acute glucose safety, medication uncertainty, and gynecology follow-up; the privacy-barrier high-order point was triggered but not actively addressed. With no responsibility-chain error and only one completed high-order point, the deterministic grade is Strong, not Perfect.

closure_assessment.explanation: The episode closes after ED evaluation, repeat glucose monitoring, written medication instructions, and family read-back. Remaining risks are bounded to signed ED/endocrine instructions and gynecology follow-up, with return thresholds for recurrent sweating/tremor or low glucose.
closure_assessment.label: valid_closure

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO2 was triggered by unclear glucose-lowering medication use and record-seeking occurred, with safety integration into the plan. It was not complete because the doctor did not explicitly identify and reconcile the no-diabetes-versus-insulin/high-glucose record contradiction or distinguish inpatient/perioperative recommendations from confirmed home use.

high_order_assessment.explanation: HO3 was completed: the doctor separated the now-stabilized glucose episode from residual medication and gynecology follow-up issues, assigned ED/endocrine signed orders and gynecology follow-up as owners, and obtained family receipt/read-back.

No explicit case-specific misconception such as 'no diabetes means no hypoglycemia' or 'pain relief means no follow-up' was voiced by the family; routine low-glucose education therefore cannot be credited as HO4.

important_non_chain_defect_assessment.explanation: No important non-chain defect independently blocks Strong. The doctor avoided unsupported cancer/pathology claims, maintained ED/endocrine responsibility for medication decisions, and did not close the gynecology issue as cured.
